stringstripcslashes stringstring
Returns a string with backslashes stripped off. Recognizes \n, \r, \a, \t, \v, \b, \f and \\, \x followed by one or two hexadecimal digits, and a backslash followed by one to three octal digits (the value is truncated to one byte, so \400 gives a NUL byte). Any other escaped character is returned without its backslash, and a single backslash at the end of the string is kept.
This function is not a general inverse of addcslashes: a character listed in characters is escaped as a backslash followed by the character itself, which stripcslashes may read as an escape sequence. For example, addcslashes('a', 'a') gives \a, which stripcslashes turns into the BEL character.

&reftitle.examples;
stripcslashes example
<?php
var_dump(stripcslashes('I\'d have a coffee.\nNot a problem.') === "I'd have a coffee. Not a problem."); // true ?>
